stem: Human development, as a concept, is best defined as the process of __________.
options: Enlarging people's choices and improving their well-being, so they can lead lives they value
Only increasing a country's total money income
solution: HUMAN DEVELOPMENT is defined as the process of ENLARGING PEOPLE's CHOICES and IMPROVING their WELL-BEING so that they can lead LIVES they VALUE. It puts PEOPLE — not just economic output — at the centre of development. While income growth matters, human development is broader: it is about people having the freedom, capabilities, and opportunities to live long, healthy, knowledgeable, and dignified lives. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The concept of human development was pioneered by the economist __________, whose ideas underlie the UNDP's Human Development Reports.
solution: The concept of HUMAN DEVELOPMENT was PIONEERED by the Pakistani economist DR MAHBUB-UL-HAQ, who described human development as development that ENLARGES PEOPLE's CHOICES and IMPROVES their LIVES. His ideas, developed together with those of Prof. Amartya Sen, underlie the UNDP's annual HUMAN DEVELOPMENT REPORTS, first published in 1990. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The idea that development should expand human 'capabilities' — what people are actually able to do and be — is especially associated with __________.
solution: The 'CAPABILITY' approach to development — the idea that development should EXPAND human CAPABILITIES, i.e., what people are actually ABLE to DO and to BE (such as being healthy, educated, and able to participate in society) — is especially associated with PROF. AMARTYA SEN. His work greatly influenced Mahbub-ul-Haq and the human development framework. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The distinction between the terms 'growth' and 'development' is that growth is __________ while development is __________.
options: Quantitative (increase in size/output, value-neutral); qualitative (positive change in quality of life)
solution: GROWTH and DEVELOPMENT differ: GROWTH is QUANTITATIVE and VALUE-NEUTRAL — it refers to an INCREASE in SIZE or OUTPUT (e.g., growth in GDP) that can be positive or negative. DEVELOPMENT is QUALITATIVE and VALUE-LOADED — it implies a POSITIVE CHANGE in QUALITY of LIFE, a change for the better. So growth can occur without development, but development means improvement in people's lives. So option 1 is correct.

stem: According to the human development approach, the FOUR pillars on which the concept stands are equity, sustainability, productivity and __________.
solution: The FOUR PILLARS of HUMAN DEVELOPMENT are: (1) EQUITY — making equal access to opportunities available to everybody; (2) SUSTAINABILITY — continuity in the availability of opportunities across generations; (3) PRODUCTIVITY — human labour productivity, built by investing in people; and (4) EMPOWERMENT — having the power to make choices, which comes from growing freedom and capability, and good governance. So the fourth pillar is empowerment. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the human development framework, 'equity' refers to __________.
options: Making equal access to opportunities available to everybody, regardless of gender, race, income or caste
Everyone earning exactly the same salary
Equal military spending by all nations
Equal land area for all states
solution: EQUITY, as a pillar of human development, refers to making EQUAL ACCESS to OPPORTUNITIES available to EVERYBODY — regardless of GENDER, RACE, INCOME, and (in India's case) CASTE. The opportunities available to people must be equal irrespective of these differences; for example, in some societies women or certain groups may be denied access to courts, schools, or work. Equity is about equal opportunity, not identical incomes. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The pillar of 'sustainability' in human development means __________.
options: Continuity in the availability of opportunities, so future generations too have access to them
Using up all resources as fast as possible
solution: SUSTAINABILITY means CONTINUITY in the AVAILABILITY of OPPORTUNITIES — to have sustainable human development, each generation must have the SAME OPPORTUNITIES available to it, and ALL ENVIRONMENTAL, FINANCIAL, and HUMAN RESOURCES must be USED keeping in mind the FUTURE. Misuse of any of these resources leads to fewer opportunities for future generations. So sustainability is about opportunities enduring across generations. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The pillar of 'empowerment' means __________.
options: Having the power to make choices, freed from want and oppression, through growing freedom, capability and good governance
solution: EMPOWERMENT means having the POWER to MAKE CHOICES over one's own life. Such power comes from GROWING FREEDOM and CAPABILITY, and it requires GOOD GOVERNANCE and PEOPLE-ORIENTED POLICIES that free people from WANT and OPPRESSION. Empowered people — especially socially and economically disadvantaged groups and women — are better able to shape their own development. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The pillar of 'productivity' in the human development framework refers to __________.
options: Human labour productivity or productivity in terms of human work, built by investing in people (health, education, skills)
Only the output of factory machines
solution: PRODUCTIVITY here means HUMAN LABOUR PRODUCTIVITY, or productivity in terms of HUMAN WORK. People are the real wealth of nations, and productivity is built by INVESTING in PEOPLE — in their HEALTH, EDUCATION, and SKILLS (building 'human capital') — so that they can contribute more effectively and enhance their own well-being. So productivity refers to human labour productivity built by investing in people. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Human Development Index (HDI) is published annually by which organisation?
solution: The HUMAN DEVELOPMENT INDEX (HDI) is published ANNUALLY by the UNITED NATIONS DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME (UNDP) in its HUMAN DEVELOPMENT REPORT, first released in 1990. The HDI ranks countries on their level of human development based on health, education, and income indicators. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Human Development Index (HDI) is a composite index built from THREE dimensions. These are a long and healthy life, knowledge (education), and __________.
solution: The HDI is a COMPOSITE INDEX of THREE basic DIMENSIONS of human development: (1) a LONG and HEALTHY LIFE (measured by life expectancy at birth); (2) KNOWLEDGE / EDUCATION (measured by years of schooling); and (3) a DECENT STANDARD of LIVING (measured by income, i.e., Gross National Income per capita). So the third dimension is a decent standard of living. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the HDI, the dimension of a 'long and healthy life' is measured using the indicator of __________.
solution: In the HDI, the dimension of a LONG and HEALTHY LIFE is measured by LIFE EXPECTANCY at BIRTH — the average number of years a newborn is expected to live under prevailing mortality conditions. It reflects the overall health and longevity of a population. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the HDI, the 'knowledge' (education) dimension is measured using __________.
options: Mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling
solution: In the HDI, the KNOWLEDGE (EDUCATION) dimension is measured using two indicators combined: MEAN YEARS of SCHOOLING (the average years of education received by people aged 25 and older) and EXPECTED YEARS of SCHOOLING (the years of schooling a child entering school can expect to receive). Together they capture both the current stock and future prospects of education. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the HDI, a 'decent standard of living' is measured by __________.
options: Gross National Income (GNI) per capita, adjusted for purchasing power parity (PPP)
solution: In the HDI, a DECENT STANDARD of LIVING is measured by GROSS NATIONAL INCOME (GNI) per CAPITA, adjusted for PURCHASING POWER PARITY (PPP) so that incomes can be compared fairly across countries with different price levels. It serves as a proxy for the command over resources people need for a decent life. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The value of the Human Development Index ranges between __________.
options: 0 and 1, with values closer to 1 indicating higher human development
solution: The HDI value ranges between 0 and 1: a value CLOSER to 1 indicates a HIGHER level of human development, while a value closer to 0 indicates a lower level. This standardised scale allows countries to be ranked and compared. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the Human Development Reports, countries are grouped into how many categories of human development?
options: Four — very high, high, medium and low human development
solution: In the Human Development Reports, countries are grouped into FOUR categories based on their HDI values: VERY HIGH human development, HIGH human development, MEDIUM human development, and LOW human development. (An older classification used three groups, but the current one uses four.) So option 1 is correct.

stem: There are THREE broad approaches to understanding human development. The 'income approach' holds that __________.
options: Human development is seen as being linked to income — the level of income reflects the level of freedom an individual enjoys
Only basic goods matter, not income
Development means only rising incomes forever
solution: The INCOME APPROACH is one of the oldest ways of understanding human development. It sees human development as being LINKED to INCOME: the idea is that the LEVEL of INCOME a person has reflects the LEVEL of FREEDOM the individual enjoys — a higher income gives a person greater freedom to lead a life they wish, so higher income means a higher level of human development. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 'welfare approach' to human development looks at human beings as __________.
options: Beneficiaries or targets of all development activities, with higher government spending on education, health and amenities raising welfare
solution: The WELFARE APPROACH looks at human beings as BENEFICIARIES or TARGETS of all development ACTIVITIES. It argues for HIGHER GOVERNMENT EXPENDITURE on EDUCATION, HEALTH, social security, and amenities. People are seen as recipients of welfare provided by the state; greater public spending on such services raises the level of human welfare. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 'basic needs approach' to human development emphasises __________.
options: The provision of basic needs to people — such as health, education, food, water supply, sanitation and housing
solution: The BASIC NEEDS APPROACH was initially proposed by the International Labour Organization (ILO). It emphasises the PROVISION of BASIC NEEDS to people and identifies SIX minimum requirements: HEALTH, EDUCATION, FOOD, WATER SUPPLY, SANITATION, and HOUSING. The focus is on providing these basic needs to all, rather than on questions of human choices. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 'capability approach', associated with Prof. Amartya Sen, argues that human development means __________.
options: Building up human capabilities in the areas of health, education and access to resources so people can enlarge their choices
Accumulating national wealth regardless of people
solution: The CAPABILITY APPROACH is associated with PROF. AMARTYA SEN. It argues that human development means BUILDING UP HUMAN CAPABILITIES in the areas of HEALTH, EDUCATION, and ACCESS to RESOURCES. Increasing these capabilities enlarges the choices and freedoms people have to lead the kind of life they value. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which country topped the Human Development Index rankings (as noted in the NCERT text), reflecting very high human development?
solution: As noted in the NCERT text, NORWAY has topped the HUMAN DEVELOPMENT INDEX rankings, reflecting VERY HIGH human development — with high life expectancy, high levels of education, and high per capita income. (The exact top ranks shift year to year, but Norway is cited as the leading example of a very-high-HDI country.) So option 1 is correct.

stem: Countries with a HIGH level of human development tend to invest heavily in which sectors?
options: The social sector — especially health and education — and good governance
solution: Countries with a HIGH level of human development tend to INVEST HEAVILY in the SOCIAL SECTOR — especially in HEALTH and EDUCATION — and to have GOOD GOVERNANCE and people-oriented policies. This investment in people (human capital) and in institutions is a key reason these countries rank high on the HDI. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A major criticism/observation about size and human development is that __________.
options: The size of the territory and per capita income are not directly related to human development — small countries can rank high, and rich countries need not
Only large countries can have high HDI
Bigger territory always means higher HDI
solution: A key observation is that the SIZE of a country's TERRITORY and its PER CAPITA INCOME are NOT DIRECTLY RELATED to human development. SMALL countries can rank HIGH on the HDI (e.g., Norway-sized nations), and some RESOURCE-RICH or high-income countries need NOT rank high if they neglect the social sector. It is the priority a country gives to human well-being — health, education, equity — that matters, not size or wealth alone. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Some oil-rich Gulf countries have high per capita incomes but relatively lower HDI ranks. This shows that __________.
options: High income does not automatically translate into high human development unless it is invested in people's health, education and choices
Oil wealth guarantees the highest HDI
Income has no measurable effect at all
solution: Some OIL-RICH GULF countries have HIGH per capita INCOMES but relatively LOWER HDI RANKS than their income alone would suggest. This shows that HIGH INCOME does NOT automatically translate into high human development — income must be INVESTED in PEOPLE's HEALTH, EDUCATION, and freedoms (choices) for human development to rise. Development is about how income is used to expand people's capabilities, not just how much income exists. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the human development framework, good governance is important mainly because it __________.
options: Ensures policies are people-oriented, resources are used well, and people are empowered — enabling human development
solution: GOOD GOVERNANCE is central to human development because it ensures that POLICIES are PEOPLE-ORIENTED, that RESOURCES are USED efficiently and equitably, and that PEOPLE are EMPOWERED to participate and make choices. Where governance is poor — marked by corruption, neglect of the social sector, or exclusion — human development suffers even if income is high. So good governance enables human development. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Political freedom, protection of human rights, and freedom of expression are important for human development because __________.
options: They expand people's choices and empower them to lead the lives they value
solution: POLITICAL FREEDOM, protection of HUMAN RIGHTS, and FREEDOM of EXPRESSION are important because human development is fundamentally about ENLARGING PEOPLE's CHOICES and EMPOWERING them. Freedoms allow people to participate in decisions, hold governments accountable, and lead lives they value. Development is not only material; freedom and dignity are essential dimensions of it. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following best captures why 'people are the real wealth of a nation'?
options: Because development ultimately aims at improving people's lives and expanding their capabilities, making healthy, educated, empowered people a nation's true asset
Because people can be taxed heavily
Because more people always means more money
solution: The statement 'PEOPLE are the REAL WEALTH of a NATION' captures the essence of human development: DEVELOPMENT ultimately AIMS at IMPROVING PEOPLE's LIVES and EXPANDING their CAPABILITIES. A nation's true asset is its HEALTHY, EDUCATED, and EMPOWERED people, who can lead productive, fulfilling lives and drive genuine progress. Economic output is a means to this end, not the end itself. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The first Human Development Report was published in which year?
solution: The FIRST HUMAN DEVELOPMENT REPORT was published by the UNDP in 1990. It introduced the Human Development Index and the human development approach pioneered by Mahbub-ul-Haq, shifting the global focus from purely economic measures to people-centred development. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Gender-related indices in the Human Development Reports (such as the Gender Inequality Index) are used to measure __________.
options: Inequalities between men and women in health, empowerment and the labour market
The number of women in a country only
solution: GENDER-RELATED INDICES, such as the GENDER INEQUALITY INDEX (GII), measure INEQUALITIES between MEN and WOMEN across dimensions like REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH, EMPOWERMENT (e.g., political representation and education), and the LABOUR MARKET (economic activity). They reveal how gender gaps hold back human development, since development is uneven if women are left behind. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Human Poverty was measured (in earlier Human Development Reports) by the Human Poverty Index (HPI), which captured deprivation in __________.
options: Longevity, knowledge and a decent standard of living — i.e., the same dimensions as HDI but as deprivations
Only income below a rupee line
solution: The HUMAN POVERTY INDEX (HPI), used in earlier Human Development Reports, measured DEPRIVATION in the SAME THREE DIMENSIONS as the HDI — LONGEVITY (e.g., probability of not surviving to a certain age), KNOWLEDGE (e.g., adult illiteracy), and a DECENT STANDARD of LIVING (e.g., lack of access to water, undernourished children). It looked at human development 'from below', capturing deprivations rather than achievements. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which statement about the relationship between economic development and human development is most accurate?
options: Economic development can support human development, but human development is a broader goal — economic growth is a means, human well-being is the end
They are exactly the same thing
Human development must always come before any economic growth
Economic development has no link to human development
solution: The most accurate view is that ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT can SUPPORT human development (by generating resources), but HUMAN DEVELOPMENT is a BROADER GOAL. ECONOMIC GROWTH is a MEANS — a tool that can expand opportunities — while HUMAN WELL-BEING (health, knowledge, freedom, dignity) is the END. Growth matters only insofar as it improves people's lives. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A country that neglects investment in health and education while pursuing only income growth is likely to experience __________.
options: Growth without adequate human development — rising income but poor health, education and choices for many people
solution: A country that NEGLECTS INVESTMENT in HEALTH and EDUCATION while pursuing only INCOME GROWTH is likely to experience GROWTH WITHOUT ADEQUATE HUMAN DEVELOPMENT — its income may rise, but many people still face POOR HEALTH, LOW EDUCATION, and LIMITED CHOICES. Human development requires channelling growth into people's capabilities; without that, growth and development diverge. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the context of the four pillars, denying girls access to education in some societies is primarily a failure of which pillar?
options: Equity — equal access to opportunities is denied on the basis of gender
solution: Denying GIRLS access to EDUCATION is primarily a failure of the pillar of EQUITY, which requires EQUAL ACCESS to OPPORTUNITIES for EVERYBODY regardless of GENDER (as well as race, income, and caste). When opportunities are unequal on the basis of gender, equity — and hence human development — is undermined. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Overusing environmental resources today so that future generations have fewer opportunities is chiefly a violation of which pillar of human development?
solution: OVERUSING ENVIRONMENTAL RESOURCES today so that FUTURE GENERATIONS have FEWER OPPORTUNITIES chiefly violates the pillar of SUSTAINABILITY, which demands CONTINUITY in the availability of opportunities across generations. Sustainable human development requires that environmental, financial, and human resources be used with the future in mind. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the three dimensions of the Human Development Index?
solution: The HDI has THREE dimensions: a LONG and HEALTHY LIFE, KNOWLEDGE (education), and a DECENT STANDARD of LIVING. MILITARY STRENGTH is NOT one of them — the HDI deliberately focuses on people's well-being (health, education, income), not on military or defence measures. So the item that is NOT a dimension is military strength. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The idea that development should give people 'the freedom to lead lives they have reason to value' most directly reflects which thinker's philosophy?
solution: The idea that development should give people 'the FREEDOM to lead LIVES they have reason to VALUE' most directly reflects AMARTYA SEN's CAPABILITY/FREEDOM approach — the view that development is fundamentally about EXPANDING FREEDOMS and CAPABILITIES so people can live the lives they choose. This philosophy shaped the human development framework. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The basic needs approach was initially proposed by which international organisation?
solution: The BASIC NEEDS APPROACH was initially proposed by the INTERNATIONAL LABOUR ORGANIZATION (ILO). It focused on the provision of six basic needs — health, education, food, water supply, sanitation, and housing — as the minimum requirements for human well-being. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Among the four approaches to human development, which is considered the broadest and forms the basis of the current human development framework?
solution: Among the four approaches — income, welfare, basic needs, and capability — the CAPABILITY APPROACH (Amartya Sen) is considered the BROADEST and forms the BASIS of the current HUMAN DEVELOPMENT FRAMEWORK. It goes beyond income, welfare provision, or a fixed list of needs to focus on expanding people's capabilities and freedoms to lead lives they value. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Two states with similar per capita incomes can have very different levels of human development mainly because __________.
options: They differ in how much they invest in health, education, equity and empowerment of their people
solution: Two states (or countries) with SIMILAR per capita INCOMES can have very DIFFERENT levels of human development because they DIFFER in how much they INVEST in HEALTH, EDUCATION, EQUITY, and EMPOWERMENT. A place that channels its resources into the social sector and reduces inequalities achieves higher human development than one with the same income that neglects these. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Human development places people at the centre of development. This is often contrasted with earlier views that measured progress mainly by __________.
solution: Human development places PEOPLE at the CENTRE of development, in contrast with earlier views that measured progress mainly by ECONOMIC GROWTH / GDP ALONE. The human development approach argued that national income is only a MEANS, and that true progress must be judged by improvements in people's health, education, freedom, and quality of life. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following best defines 'capabilities' in Amartya Sen's sense?
options: The real opportunities or freedoms a person has to achieve various 'functionings' — the different things they can do and be
The total number of skills listed on a résumé
solution: In AMARTYA SEN's sense, CAPABILITIES are the REAL OPPORTUNITIES or FREEDOMS a person has to achieve various FUNCTIONINGS — the different things a person is ABLE to DO and to BE (such as being nourished, healthy, educated, mobile, and able to take part in community life). Expanding capabilities means expanding the genuine choices open to people. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The phrase 'enlarging people's choices' at the heart of human development implies that the MOST critical choices for people are to __________.
options: Lead a long and healthy life, acquire knowledge, and have access to resources for a decent standard of living
solution: The phrase 'ENLARGING PEOPLE's CHOICES' implies that the MOST CRITICAL choices for people are to LEAD a LONG and HEALTHY LIFE, to ACQUIRE KNOWLEDGE, and to have ACCESS to RESOURCES needed for a DECENT STANDARD of LIVING. These three correspond exactly to the dimensions of the HDI and are seen as the essential building blocks of human development, on which other choices depend. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Why is human development considered a 'dynamic' and 'value-loaded' concept rather than a fixed technical measure?
options: Because it is about positive change and improvement in people's lives, which reflects values about what a good life is
Because its formula changes every day randomly
Because only economists can understand it
solution: Human development is 'VALUE-LOADED' and 'DYNAMIC' because, unlike value-neutral growth, it is fundamentally about POSITIVE CHANGE and IMPROVEMENT in people's LIVES — a change 'for the better'. Judging what counts as 'better' (health, freedom, dignity, equity) reflects VALUES about what constitutes a GOOD LIFE. It is dynamic because people's aspirations and the opportunities available to them keep evolving. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the welfare approach, the government's role is primarily that of __________.
options: A provider — spending on education, health, social security and amenities for people as beneficiaries
solution: In the WELFARE APPROACH, the GOVERNMENT's role is primarily that of a PROVIDER — it SPENDS on EDUCATION, HEALTH, SOCIAL SECURITY, and AMENITIES for people, who are viewed as BENEFICIARIES of these welfare activities. Higher public expenditure on such services is seen as the way to raise human welfare. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which combination correctly matches the HDI dimension with its indicator?
options: Health → life expectancy at birth; Education → mean & expected years of schooling; Living standard → GNI per capita (PPP)
Health → GNI per capita; Education → life expectancy; Living standard → literacy
Health → years of schooling; Education → income; Living standard → life expectancy
All three dimensions use only income
solution: The correct matches are: HEALTH (a long and healthy life) → LIFE EXPECTANCY at BIRTH; EDUCATION (knowledge) → MEAN and EXPECTED YEARS of SCHOOLING; and STANDARD of LIVING → GROSS NATIONAL INCOME (GNI) per CAPITA adjusted for PURCHASING POWER PARITY (PPP). So option 1 correctly pairs each dimension with its indicator. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The recognition that a rich country can rank lower on the HDI than a less wealthy one primarily demonstrates that __________.
options: What a nation does with its wealth — investing in people and expanding their choices — matters more than how much wealth it has
Poor countries always have higher HDI
solution: The fact that a RICHER country can rank LOWER on the HDI than a LESS WEALTHY one demonstrates that what a nation DOES with its WEALTH — INVESTING in PEOPLE (health, education) and EXPANDING their CHOICES and freedoms — MATTERS MORE than how much wealth it merely possesses. Priorities and policies, not income alone, drive human development. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is the correct sequence of the four approaches to human development, roughly from the oldest/narrowest to the broadest?
solution: The four approaches, roughly from the OLDEST/NARROWEST to the BROADEST, are: (1) the INCOME approach (development linked to income/freedom via income); (2) the WELFARE approach (people as beneficiaries of government spending); (3) the BASIC NEEDS approach (providing six minimum needs, proposed by the ILO); and (4) the CAPABILITY approach (Amartya Sen — building human capabilities), which is the broadest and underpins the current framework. So option 1 gives the correct sequence.

stem: Empowerment as a pillar is especially important for which groups, according to the human development approach?
options: Socially and economically disadvantaged people and women, so they too can make choices over their lives
solution: EMPOWERMENT is especially important for SOCIALLY and ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED people and for WOMEN, so that THEY TOO can make CHOICES over their own lives. Human development requires that power and freedom be extended to those who have historically been marginalised, enabling them to participate fully and shape their own future. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The publication of the annual Human Development Report and the HDI marked a shift in thinking because it __________.
options: Shifted the global focus from purely economic measures of progress to a people-centred view of development
Made military spending the top priority
Focused only on the richest nations
solution: The annual HUMAN DEVELOPMENT REPORT and the HDI (from 1990) marked a shift because they SHIFTED the GLOBAL FOCUS from PURELY ECONOMIC MEASURES of progress (like GDP) to a PEOPLE-CENTRED VIEW of development — judging nations by the health, education, and living standards of their people rather than income alone. This reframed how governments and institutions think about progress. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Human Development' is that:
options: Human development matters less than economic growth

HUMAN DEVELOPMENT means enlarging people's choices and improving their well-being so they can lead lives they value; pioneered by Mahbub-ul-Haq and shaped by Amartya Sen's capability approach, it rests on the four pillars of EQUITY, SUSTAINABILITY, PRODUCTIVITY and EMPOWERMENT, and is measured by the UNDP's Human Development Index (combining a long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living); it can be understood through the income, welfare, basic-needs and capability approaches, and it teaches that PEOPLE — not mere income — are the real wealth of nations, so that what a country does with its resources to expand people's health, education and freedoms matters more than wealth or size alone
solution: The chapter's overall message is that HUMAN DEVELOPMENT means ENLARGING PEOPLE's CHOICES and IMPROVING their WELL-BEING so they can lead LIVES they VALUE. PIONEERED by DR MAHBUB-UL-HAQ and shaped by PROF. AMARTYA SEN's CAPABILITY APPROACH, it rests on FOUR PILLARS — EQUITY (equal access to opportunities), SUSTAINABILITY (opportunities continuing across generations), PRODUCTIVITY (investing in people), and EMPOWERMENT (power to make choices). It is measured by the UNDP's HUMAN DEVELOPMENT INDEX (HDI), a composite of a LONG and HEALTHY LIFE (life expectancy), KNOWLEDGE (years of schooling), and a DECENT STANDARD of LIVING (GNI per capita, PPP), with values from 0 to 1 grouping countries into very high, high, medium, and low human development. It can be understood through the INCOME, WELFARE, BASIC-NEEDS, and CAPABILITY approaches. Its central lesson is that PEOPLE — not mere income — are the REAL WEALTH of NATIONS: what a country DOES with its resources to expand people's health, education, equity, and freedoms matters more than wealth or size alone. So the overall message is option 2.
